newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - EU institutions conducive to stable Euro.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - EU institutions conducive to stable Euro.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Friday the institutional preconditions for creating a stable euro were favourable but warned against attempts to influence the European Central Bank.
Tietmeyer said the euro had to be stable to be a success and that a soft euro would place a heavy burden on European integration.

"The foundation must be solid and sustainably strong from the start to make the currency union resilient and weatherproof, because in monetary policy too, the honeymoon of the beginning often rapidly ends," Tietmeyer said according to the text of a speech to a conference in Montreux, Switzerland.
The speech was made available ahead of delivery.
"Under the Maastricht Treaty the task of the future European monetary policy is simple: to secure price stability," Tietmeyer said.
"Europe's monetary policy will also be given added support from the Stability and Growth Pact. The institutional preconditions for a stable euro are therefore favourable."

"But what is decisive in the end is how the framework is filled via political decisions. This applies to the choice of member countries and in particular to the concrete shaping of monetary policy in the currency union.

"One must urgently warn against attempts to polticise the European Central Bank or drive it off its course of stability. They would in the end extract the high price of a loss of confidence, capital outflows and rising interest rates."
